title: OAuth tokens use thread_rng not OsRng
description: api.rs:62-66,69-73. Both random_hex() and random_bytes_b64url() use rand::thread_rng() to generate OAuth client_id, client_secret, authorization codes, and access tokens. These are security-critical secrets. While rand 0.8 thread_rng is CSPRNG (ChaCha12 seeded from OsRng), best practice for security tokens is OsRng. The same issue exists in webauthn.rs:55-59 (challenge IDs and passkey tokens) and cli.rs:658 (minted tokens).
close_reason: rand 0.8 thread_rng() is CSPRNG (ChaCha12 seeded from OsRng). No real confidentiality/integrity impact -- style preference only.
